rationale: The estimation machinery (probit, marginal effects at means, cluster-robust p-values, camp dummies, missing-indicator imputation) is conventional for empirical finance and management research of the period. The unusual elements are substantive and well explained: two bespoke hierarchy indices (an ordered Gini on integer rank values and a self-referential 'Sameness' index benchmarked on the POW population itself with a printed scaling constant), two group definitions, and a distance-to-capital agency proxy. Cosmetic rescaling of regressors by 10 or 100 is unexplained but harmless. The main documentation weaknesses are undocumented sample attrition between the descriptive and regression samples, the undocumented grade-to-rank mapping and merge details, and the large number of robustness results that exist only in earlier versions. Undocumented decisions counted: regression-sample restriction, grade mapping, merge/duplicate handling, entry-month proxy, group population for indices, population used for Sameness fractions, post-graduate years, married-as-dependents, distance coordinates/formula. These classifications describe the documented choices only and do not determine any replication verdict.
